issues.sym: The brake pedal goes down but the car does not slow, with little or no warning.
issues.why: A retainer that holds the brake pedal pushrod could be missing or not seated, letting the pedal separate from the brake booster. GM recalled these cars.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until you confirm this recall is done. Check your VIN right away.

issues.sym: The passenger airbag off/on indicator shows the wrong status for who is in the seat, or an airbag warning light.
issues.why: The passenger sensing system could turn the front passenger airbag off when it should be on, or on when it should be off. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have it done. Keep children in the back seat until it is fixed.

issues.t: Ignition key can slip out of Run
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, especially over bumps or with a heavy key ring, and steering and brakes suddenly feel heavy.
issues.why: The ignition key can be bumped out of the Run position. That cuts engine power and power assist and can stop the airbags from deploying. This was part of GM's large ignition key recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Until it is done, use only the key with nothing else on the ring.

issues.sym: Low beams flicker or will not come on while the high beams still work.
issues.why: The headlight driver module that switches the low beams can overheat and fail. GM recalled these cars to fix it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the headlamp recall. Avoid night driving until the low beams work reliably.

issues.sym: Oil level drops between changes, a low oil light, blue smoke, or spark plug fouling and misfires.
issues.why: The piston rings on this engine can fail to seal well, letting oil burn in the cylinders. GM issued a bulletin with an oil use test and a new piston and ring kit.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and top it off. Ask a dealer to run the oil consumption test from the bulletin.

issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing codes, a rattle at cold start, long cranking, or rough running.
issues.why: The timing chains on this V6 can wear and stretch, made worse by low oil or long oil change intervals. GM released timing chain kits for the repair.
issues.next: Get timing codes checked promptly. A stretched chain can jump and badly damage the engine, so avoid long trips until it is inspected.

issues.t: Rear toe links rust and break
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the car pulling or wandering, or rear tires wearing oddly.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, the rear toe links can corrode and snap, which makes the car harder to control. GM recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the toe link recall. Stop driving if the rear end suddenly feels loose.

issues.t: Power seat height bolt can fall out
issues.sym: The driver or passenger power seat suddenly drops or rocks, or a rattle from under the seat.
issues.why: A bolt in the power seat height adjuster can work loose and fall out, letting the seat drop. GM recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the seat recall and have it repaired.

issues.sym: A service battery charging system message, a drained 12V battery, or a no-start.
issues.why: The generator control module in the mild-hybrid system can fail. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the eAssist recall and have a dealer diagnose the charging system.

issues.t: Wrong brake rotors on the front
issues.sym: Longer stopping distances or brakes that feel weak.
issues.why: Some cars were built with thinner rear rotors installed at the front, which reduces braking performance. GM recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have the rotors inspected before relying on the brakes.

issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some cars may show an airbag light.
issues.why: The airbag computer could run a self-test at the wrong moment and fail to deploy the front airbags in a crash. GM recalled the cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the airbag software recall and get it done.

issues.t: Water can get into power steering connectors
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets heavy, with a power steering warning message.
issues.why: Wiring connectors for the electric power steering may let water in, which can cut power steering assist. GM recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If steering gets heavy, slow down and get the car looked at before driving further.

issues.sym: The car pulls or feels unstable, or the rear tires wear unevenly.
issues.why: The rear toe links on some cars were installed incorrectly at the factory, which can affect handling. GM recalled them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the toe link recall and have it repaired.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper pistons can corrode
issues.sym: Rear brakes dragging, grinding, or reduced braking.
issues.why: Some rear caliper pistons were built without their protective coating, so they can corrode and stop working properly. GM recalled the cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the caliper recall and have the rear brakes inspected.

issues.t: Start/stop accumulator cover can leak fluid
issues.sym: Transmission fluid leaking under the car, slipping, or the car losing drive.
issues.why: The end cap on the transmission's start/stop accumulator may be missing bolts, so it can come loose and fluid can leak out. GM recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. Stop driving if you see transmission fluid leaking or the car starts slipping.
